scenario: Out-of-order append — second entry has an earlier timestamp than the first, AND references a causal_parent_id that does not exist anywhere in the log
note: append() currently performs NO validation of (a) timestamp monotonicity or (b) whether causal_parent_id refers to an entry that actually exists in the log. Both were silently accepted; verifyChain() still reports valid because the hash chain is computed from append-call order, not from timestamp or causal_parent_id. This is an integration gap between two individually-reasonable pieces: the hash chain guarantees append-order integrity, but causal_parent_id is currently decorative — nothing enforces it references a real prior entry. Logged as SDB-GAR-03 (Type II gap) — a Decision Record is needed on whether GARLog should validate causal_parent_id referential integrity and/or timestamp ordering at append() time, or whether this is left to a higher layer (e.g. SOV Event Stream).
